title: Water Watch Center says it is giving water utilities in 26 states free security monitoring
date_note: Cybersecurity Dive (23 Nov) says the group announced it on Friday, which is 20 November (the article, published Monday 23 Nov, gives no calendar date).
org: Water Watch Center (National Rural Water Association and DEF CON Franklin)
summary: Cybersecurity Dive reports that the Water Watch Center, a joint effort of the National Rural Water Association and DEF CON Franklin, says it is providing free security monitoring and assistance to water utilities in 26 states so far. The center pays technology and cybersecurity firms for the intrusion detection services and consultations. Cybersecurity Dive says nearly 100 utilities have contacted it; Nextgov says more than 100 have expressed interest.
plain: A water-sector group says it is giving free cybersecurity monitoring and help to water utilities in 26 states.
exec: Free monitoring is on offer to US water utilities, a sector the report says Iran-linked hackers breached over the summer.
impact: Free intrusion detection and defensive consultations for participating utilities.

evidence.quote: providing free security monitoring and assistance to water utilities in 26 states so far
Nearly 100 utilities have contacted the center to inquire about its services, the group said.
more than 100 water and wastewater utilities, which all serve populations of 10,000 people or fewer, have expressed an interest

validation.note: Cybersecurity Dive and Nextgov each state the 26-state figure; they differ on how many utilities made contact (nearly 100 vs more than 100).

review.note: date: Friday in a Monday 23 Nov article is 20 Nov, not 21 Nov
